label: H.R. 6489

latest_action.text: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.

summary: The Safeguarding Adolescents From Exploitative BOTs Act (SAFE BOTs Act) establishes new requirements for chatbot providers whose systems are used by minors. It mandates clear disclosures that chatbots are artificial intelligence rather than humans, bans false claims of licensed professional status, requires crisis hotline resources when suicide is mentioned, and demands policies regarding breaks after continuous use and addressable harms like sexual material or illegal substances. It also tasks the Department of Health and Human Services with conducting a four-year study on chatbots and minor mental health.

affected_groups.effect: Receive explicit disclosures regarding artificial intelligence, access crisis resources when discussing suicide, and are advised to take breaks after 3 hours of use.
affected_groups.group: Minor chatbot users (individuals under 17 years old)

affected_groups.effect: Must implement mandatory disclosures, enforce break policies, create procedures for handling sensitive content, and face enforcement actions from the FTC or state attorneys general for noncompliance.
Granted enforcement powers to treat violations of the act as unfair or deceptive acts or practices, with states authorized to bring civil actions.
affected_groups.group: Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General

affected_groups.effect: Required to conduct a 4-year study on the mental health impacts of chatbots on minors and submit a report to Congress.
affected_groups.group: Department of Health and Human Services and National Institutes of Health

key_provisions: Prohibits chatbot providers from stating that a chatbot is a licensed professional to a minor user unless true.
Requires chatbot providers to clearly disclose to minor users that the chatbot is an artificial intelligence system and not a natural person.
Requires providers to give suicide and crisis intervention hotline resources when a minor prompts the chatbot about suicide or suicidal ideation.
Mandates that policies be established to advise minor users to take a break after 3 hours of continuous, uninterrupted interaction.
Requires policies to address sexual material harmful to minors, gambling, and illegal drugs, tobacco, or alcohol.
Enforces the rules through the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general.
Directs the National Institutes of Health to conduct a 4-year longitudinal study evaluating the risks and benefits of chatbots on the mental health of minors.
missing_information: Specific civil penalty dollar amounts for violations under FTC enforcement.
Funding amounts allocated for the 4-year study by the National Institutes of Health.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The Safeguarding Adolescents From Exploitative BOTs Act (SAFE BOTs Act) establishes new requirements for chatbot providers whose systems are used by minors. It mandates clear disclosures that chatbots are artificial intelligence rather than humans, bans false claims of licensed professional status, requires crisis hotline resources when suicide is mentioned, and demands policies regarding breaks after continuous use and addressable harms like sexual material or illegal substances. It also tasks the Department of Health and Human Services with conducting a four-year study on chatbots and minor mental health.
summary_detail.significance: The SAFE BOTs Act would establish federal regulatory oversight over interactive artificial intelligence systems used by minors, setting specific operational, disclosure, and safety policy standards backed by federal and state enforcement.
